author: Mymy220AKAMimi
title: This Subscription Is A Scam For Light Users
content:
I rarely print and only need to replace my ink cartridges about once a year. Paying $7.99 per month for HP Instant Ink adds up to $95.88 a year, which is more than it would cost me to simply buy replacement cartridges myself.

I decided to cancel my subscription with 100 pages remaining for the month (and realistically, it should have been more since unused pages from previous months weren’t used at all) and I still have full ink cartridges still installed. After canceling, HP informed me that the Instant Ink cartridges would be disabled, meaning I could no longer use the ink I had already paid for. To print again, I now have to spend about $69 on regular, non-HP InstaInk cartridges.

That is a scam. I paid for the subscription, and the cartridges are still full, yet HP remotely blocks them from working once you cancel. To make matters worse, I couldn’t even remove my credit card information from the app.

If you print a high volume of pages every month, Instant Ink might make sense. But if you’re a light user, you’re likely to spend far more than necessary. You’re better off buying regular cartridges when you actually need them. Because of this experience, I won’t be purchasing HP products ever again.

title: A Printing App That Makes Its Own Print Menu Unreadable
content:
This app is astonishingly bad at the one thing it is supposed to do: print.

On an iPhone in Dark Mode, the print-options menu can display white text on a white background, making the controls completely unreadable. That is not a minor cosmetic glitch. It makes the app functionally unusable. The official workaround is apparently to change the appearance setting for the entire phone just to use HP’s app, which is absurd.

HP has had ample time and resources to fix a basic interface defect that should never have passed quality control in the first place. Instead, customers who already paid for HP hardware are left troubleshooting an app that cannot reliably display its own menus.

A printer app should make printing easier. This one adds frustration, wastes time, and reflects an embarrassing lack of attention to basic usability.

author: Keither44
title: New 2026 HP Envy printer vs old 2018? Envy HP printer
content:
I’ve delayed getting a new printer for the last couple of years because the old one worked so well. But since the old one is no longer supported by HP, although it still worked fine, I bought this new one.

What a dramatic improvement in technology!

What I expected to be a complicated new printer setup, whatever complications are objectively inherent in it, all I had to do was push one button at a time and response to a single instruction at a time.

After around 15 of these pushes, the printer set up is completely resolved, and has just enabled me to seamlessly print from even my iPhone for the first time!

The voice recognition system has so far been exactly accurate! What a wonderful addition to the experience!

As a partially literate, 81-year-old printer enthusiast, I’m astonished at this “new“ innovation.

My longtime, unfailing faith in HP has been confirmed yet again.

Thanks to all the engineers, technicians, marketers, and other members of your corporation’s staff for bringing me this culminating pleasure to smooth out my last years of life.

What would we do without each other – the product producers and their grateful consumers?

Thanks to all of you for such a wonderful product!
